title: Crunchyroll Reveals English Dub Casts for Full Clearing Another World Under a Goddess with Zero Believers, 2 More Anime
content:
Crunchyroll began streaming the English dub for The Prince of Tennis II U-17 World Cup: Final Member Selection Match ( Shin Tennis no Ōji-sama U-17 World Cup Kesshō Member Ketteisen ), the sequel anime to The Prince of Tennis II: U-17 World Cup Semifinal ( Shin Tennis no Ōji-sama U-17 World Cup Semifinal ) anime, on Friday.

The company also began streaming the English dub for the second season of the television anime based on Nana Mikoshiba 's The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World ( Hyōken no Majutsushi ga Sekai wo Suberu - Sekai Saikyō no Majutsushi de Aru Shōnen wa, Majutsu Gakuin ga Nyūgaku Suru ) light novel series on the same day.

In addition, Crunchyroll will begin streaming an English dub for the television anime of Isle Osaki 's Full Clearing Another World under a Goddess with Zero Believers ( Shinja Zero no Megami-sama to Hajimeru Isekai Kōryaku ) light novel series on Sunday.

title: Land of the Lustrous' Haruko Ichikawa Launches New Manga Cosmic Mimimi
content:
The December issue of Kodansha 's monthly Afternoon magazine announced on Friday Haruko Ichikawa will launch a new series titled Cosmic Mimimi in the next issue on November 25.

The "neo kawaii sci-fi" series follows Mimimi, who lives in a "cool" and "dreaming" city. Its goal is to make everyone happy. Strange and happy things are sure to occur around this creature of happiness.

Ichikawa launched Land of the Lustrous in Kodansha 's Afternoon magazine in 2012. Kodansha published the 13th and final compiled book volume in November 2024. The manga ended in April 2024.

Kodansha USA Publishing is releasing the manga in English.

The 12-episode anime adaptation of the manga premiered in October 2017. HIDIVE streamed the series outside of the United States and Canada as it aired, and added the anime for the United States and Canada starting in June 2018. Amazon's now-defunct Anime Strike service streamed the series in the United States and Canada as it aired. Sentai Filmworks released the anime in a steelbook complete collection in January 2019.

The Science Fiction & Fantasy Writers of Japan gave Land of the Lustrous the grand prize in the group's 45th Nihon SF Taishō Awards in 2025.

The Japanese Association for Gender, Fantasy, & Science Fiction awarded the manga the top prize in the Sense of Gender Awards in August 2025.

title: Tougen Anki: Nikko Kegon Falls Arc Anime Gets English Dub on Crunchyroll
content:
Crunchyroll announced on Saturday that it is now streaming an English dub for the first two episodes of the Tougen Anki: Nikko Kegon Falls Arc television anime based on Yura Urushibara 's Tougen Anki: Legend of the Cursed Blood manga. The announcement did not mention the English dub cast.

The anime debuted on television on October 2 and on streaming services outside Japan on October 2 at 25:00 JST (effectively October 3 at 1:00 a.m.).

REMOW describes the new arc:

Having survived the fierce battles in Kyoto and Nerima, Shiki and his fellow students at Rasetsu Academy are steadily growing stronger. But Yaoroshi rejects Mudano's lessons on the importance of friendship. Drawn to Oni Brigade General Hayate Todoroki's call for “the total eradication of the Momotaro,” he leaves the academy. When Shiki realizes that the Oni Brigade's creed makes even noncombatants targets for slaughter, he sets out after Yaoroshi with Mudano and the other students. Their destination is Nikko, where Kegon Falls stopped flowing some time ago, and a massive research facility has since been built. Within its walls, horrific experiments are underway...

The Tougen Anki anime debuted in July 2025. The "Nerima Arc" began in October 2025.

The anime streams outside Japan on the following platforms: Crunchyroll , Netflix , Prime Video, Samsung TV Plus , Anime Onegai , Bandplay , ADN , ANIME GENERATION , Anime Key, iQIYI international, bilibili (Bstation), Laftel , Bahamut, My-Video , 中華電信MOD, HamiVideo, KKTV, friDay, LINE TV, ANIWON, ANIBOX , TVING , WAVVE , LAFTEL , WATCHA PLAY, KT genieTV, SK BTV , and LG U+TV.

On Prime Video, the series is available worldwide except in Japan and Mainland China, and on Netflix the series is available worldwide outside of Japan. Crunchyroll is also releasing an English dub for the series.

The anime also has a mini companion anime titled Onimomomomo . The staff released the episodes weekly alongside the main episodes.

Ato Nonaka is directing the anime at Studio Hibari . Hiroyuki Hashimoto is the assistant director. Yukie Sugawara ( The Idolm@ster SideM , No Guns Life , The Unwanted Undead Adventurer ) is writing and supervising the anime's scripts. Ryoko Amisaki ( Kino's Journey - the Beautiful World- ) is designing the characters. Hiroyuki Becchaku is the art designer, while Scott MacDonald is directing the art. Saki Tada is the color key artist. Naoki Serizawa is the compositing director of photography. Ryota Fukushima is directing the CG. Yumika Okazaki is editing. Satoki Iida is directing the sound, and Kohta Yamamoto is composing the music. Pony Canyon is credited for the music production.

Urushibara launched the manga in Akita Publishing 's Weekly Shōnen Champion magazine in June 2020. The 30th compiled book volume shipped on July 8. Yen Press began publishing the manga in English in September 2024, and it will release the sixth volume on November 24.

The manga previously inspired a stage play that ran Tokyo and Osaka in February 2024, and a sequel stage play ran in January 2025.

title: Dragon Ball’s Biggest Mistake Was Not Making Gohan the Strongest & Here’s Why
content:
The unlikeliest of Saiyans became its most powerful in Dragon Ball , when the kind-hearted Goku began a never-ending journey to the top of the power ladder. Vegeta follows so closely behind that it never lets Goku rest on his laurels, and with the introduction of Broly the above statement is certainly in question, as he’s proven to be extremely formidable too. Whatever the case may be, one character never reached his full potential and that’s Gohan.

This story would’ve kicked off in the Cell Saga and never stopped had Gohan continued training. The young Saiyan was only a child when he first attained Super Saiyan 2 and obliterated Cell. At the time no one could match his ability, but in just a few short years Gohan became a scholar and stopped his training. He’s had a few moments where he’s been called back to the battlefield since though. The momentum he had came to an abrupt halt after the Cell Saga, however, and Gohan could’ve been truly great in an another timeline.

Gohan Gives Goku A Run For His Money At Different Points

Goku never asked for someone else to take up the mantle as the Universe 7 defender , but his son did help accomplish such a feat before he was called upon against Perfect Cell. The start of his martial arts’ career came out of necessity when his father was killed in the Saiyan Saga, and then Gohan is quickly trained under the tutelage of Piccolo. He learns quickly and is an asset, despite his youthfulness, in stalling Frieza long enough to get Goku back into the fight and to ultimately defeat him. It’s just more evidence that Gohan could’ve elevated into the stratosphere had he not stopped.

In the Cell Saga, it’s learned that Gohan is an even more kind-hearted Saiyan than his father. Now in fairness, Gohan is still a child in many ways but has grown up quite fast, as he’s seen multiple violent acts against his friends and family. It only took one final button push from Cell to bring the rage necessary for Gohan to ascend to Super Saiyan 2 and tear Cell limb from limb with a Kamehameha. His maturity, controlled aggression and fast learning set him up to be a better fighter than Goku . However, he became a diligent student, then dutiful husband and father.

He got rusty and stopped leveling up as a result, but it wasn’t the last time he was needed. It seemed time and time again that Gohan could tap into his power when the situation called for it. The lull falls in about this time. His relationship with Videl is explored, his superhero phase as The Great Saiyaman occurred and he attended high school. There’s a lot of lost time where he could’ve stacked training days. Now, Goku obviously stopped training long enough to have a family with Chi-Chi, albeit he’s never around much after. Still, Gohan could’ve become a doting husband and father, but maybe put the books down more and taken his father’s route to greatness.

Gohan Could Have Gone a Much Different Route

Nevertheless, Gohan moved on and managed to defeat a number of fighters in the Tournament of Power and even got back into shape while training with Piccolo. Gohan made the switch pretty easily, but even in that instance, it wasn’t all on his shoulders. To that point, he’d only defeated one major villain in the series – that situation would soon change. However, it just proves that his accelerated skill set could carry a long way, even on short notice.

In Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero , the movie acknowledges the debate. Pan asks Piccolo if Gohan could be stronger than Goku if he wanted to be. Piccolo answers that at one time he could be, but he wasn’t sure anymore. Still, his mentor then stated that when the time would come for Gohan to step up he’d find a way. It’s Gohan’s time to shine front and center of this film, and the nostalgia-boost hits a lot harder this time as Cell Max learns. A callback to Android 16’s head getting smashed, Gohan finds out that Pan has been kidnapped by the Red Ribbon Army, and he snaps. Within one turn, he explodes into a Super Saiyan and gets right back to his old ways.

And almost as a full-circle moment, he has to face a different iteration of the villain he defeated to become the strongest Saiyan at that time. After accessing “Gohan Beast” he literally splits Cell Max’s head in half with a Special Beam Cannon . And for the thousandth time in Dragon Ball history, Gohan goes from nerd to world saver in just a few short moments. Since the series decided to create a multiverse, it’s worth exploring the what-if involving Gohan.

Will we get a world where he keeps training and becomes a Super Saiyan 3 first before his father? Also, what kind of different transformations could he achieve if he went to train with Beerus, Whis, Vegeta and his father? The story is loaded up with a lot of different outcomes, but the series has explored plenty of fun plot lines here recently – why not this one? Do you think Dragon Ball should branch off and create a what-if timeline for the son of the world’s greatest Saiyan? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: 3 Anime to Watch If You Miss Dr. Stone
content:
Dr. Stone confirmed its anime sequel only a few months after the series wrapped up its main story. The anime reached its conclusion in June this year, seven years after its premiere. The series is based on an award-winning manga written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Boichi, which began serialization in Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in 2017. Although the finale unraveled the mystery behind the petrification, it also had an open-ended conclusion after Senku announced he would build a time machine to stop the tragedy from 3700 years ago. There’s no denying that Dr. Stone is one of the most beloved series of all time.

Thanks to its unique premise and sci-fi elements, which are rare to see in Shonen, the anime gained enough popularity to not only adapt the entire story but also confirm a sequel. Dr. Stone Terraforming was announced this month as an official sequel to the main story. It’s based on a short manga sequel titled Dr. Stone: 4D Science , to give a brief glimpse at the characters’ journey after the ending. Since the sequel is only three chapters long, it couldn’t be compiled in one volume, but all chapters are available to read on the official website of Viz Media. Although the anime sequel will take a while before its premiere, fans can watch these three shows in the meantime.

3) Ascendance of a Bookworm

While the setting of both stories couldn’t be more different, the protagonists have the same goal of using modern knowledge to rebuild and innovate low-tech society. This isekai follows Urano Motosu, who loves books more than anything. Just when she was about to start her dream job of becoming a librarian, she died in an accident before waking up in an unknown world as Myne, a frail five-year-old girl. However, although she got a second chance at life, she is frustrated by the lack of books in the world since there’s no printing press. Not only that, but books have to be written and copied by hand; they are so expensive that only nobles can afford them. And thus begins Myne’s journey as a bookworm as she strives to read and make more books so everyone can have access to them. The anime concluded its Season 4 in early October 2026 before announcing a sequel season.

2) Cells at Work!

Another anime with a different setting than Dr. Stone , but what makes Cells at Work! truly stand out is how it turns human biology into a workplace drama. Both stories use real-world science, chemistry, and biology as their core narrative while also keeping the story entertaining for viewers of all ages. The protagonist in the anime is literally a human cell given a personality. The story takes place inside a human body where roughly 37.2 trillion cells work nonstop to keep the person alive. Sekkekkyuu AE3803 is a cheerful airhead who is fresh out of training, and it’s more than ready to do the important task of transporting oxygen. On the other hand, Hakkekkyuu U-1146 continues to work hard to eliminate foreign bacteria that want to make the body their new lair. Even the little platelets line up for a new construction project. The anime released two seasons, but it hasn’t fully adapted the manga yet. While the second season released eight episodes in 2021, a sequel hasn’t been confirmed so far.

1) Astra Lost in Space

Just like Dr. Stone , this sci-fi anime also takes place in the far future , where nine children find themselves lost in space on a field trip gone wrong. Since the story is set in the future, it’s set in a world where space venturing is so common that even high school students are able to do it. Both anime focus on problem-solving and using whatever limited resources they have available to them. After being stranded, the group of teenagers finds an abandoned spaceship they name the Astra allows them to make the long trip home. However, it doesn’t take long for them to slowly uncover the conspiracy behind what happened to them and their world. The anime only released one season, but that’s all it needed to portray an exceptionally well-written story. The series is praised for its concise plot, solid character development throughout the series, and intriguing depiction of adventure through the lens of high school students.

The anime reached its conclusion in June this year, seven years after its premiere. The series is based on an award-winning manga written by Riichiro Inagaki and illustrated by Boichi, which began serialization in Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in 2017. Although the finale unraveled the mystery behind the petrification, it also had an open-ended conclusion after Senku announced he would build a time machine to stop the tragedy from 3700 years ago. There’s no denying that Dr. Stone is one of the most beloved series of all time.

Thanks to its unique premise and sci-fi elements, which are rare to see in Shonen, the anime gained enough popularity to not only adapt the entire story but also confirm a sequel. Dr. Stone Terraforming was announced this month as an official sequel to the main story. It’s based on a short manga sequel titled Dr. Stone: 4D Science , to give a brief glimpse at the characters’ journey after the ending. Since the sequel is only three chapters long, it couldn’t be compiled in one volume, but all chapters are available to read on the official website of Viz Media. Although the anime sequel will take a while before its premiere, fans can watch these three shows in the meantime.

While the setting of both stories couldn’t be more different, the protagonists have the same goal of using modern knowledge to rebuild and innovate low-tech society. This isekai follows Urano Motosu, who loves books more than anything. Just when she was about to start her dream job of becoming a librarian, she died in an accident before waking up in an unknown world as Myne, a frail five-year-old girl. However, although she got a second chance at life, she is frustrated by the lack of books in the world since there’s no printing press. Not only that, but books have to be written and copied by hand; they are so expensive that only nobles can afford them. And thus begins Myne’s journey as a bookworm as she strives to read and make more books so everyone can have access to them. The anime concluded its Season 4 in early October 2026 before announcing a sequel season.

Both stories use real-world science, chemistry, and biology as their core narrative while also keeping the story entertaining for viewers of all ages. Sekkekkyuu AE3803 is a cheerful airhead who is fresh out of training, and it’s more than ready to do the important task of transporting oxygen. On the other hand, Hakkekkyuu U-1146 continues to work hard to eliminate foreign bacteria that want to make the body their new lair. Even the little platelets line up for a new construction project. title: Netflix’s One Piece Star Drops Ominous Season 3 Tease: “My Plan Unfolds”
content:
One Piece is now in the works on the third season of its live-action series coming to Netflix next year, and the star behind Crocodile is readying fans for his return in the new episodes with an ominous tease. One Piece has really been a monster hit with Netflix ever since the live-action series first made its debut with the streaming service, and it’s bound to get even bigger with the upcoming debut of its third season taking on the biggest arc yet from Eiichiro Oda’s original manga.

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta will be making its premiere with Netflix sometime next year, and it will be adapting the Alabasta Saga from Eiichiro Oda’s original manga. After making its introductory appearance in the live-action series at the end of the second season, Joe Manganiello teased his return for the third season in an ominous way with a recent appearance on The Tonight Show With Jimmy Fallon, “And then my plan unfolds…”

Joe Manganiello Teases Crocodile Return in Netflix’s One Piece Season 3

“I’m at the very end…you find out in Season 2 that all these things are happening, you don’t know who’s behind it, ” Manganiello explained about his involvement with Netflix’s One Piece live-action series thus far. “Then at the end it’s me. And then Season 3, which we just spent six months shooting in Cape Town, South Africa, will come out some time next year. And then my plan unfolds.” It’s not much of a tease, but it further emphasizes just how much bigger of a role that Crocodile is going to have in the coming season.

Manganiello might have only been briefly seen at the end of the second season to tease Crocodile’s main villain role for the Alabasta arc, but he’s been ominously teasing the third season through the promotional materials thus far. Previously revealing earlier this Summer, “Nakama, put on your seatbelts and get ready, ’cause you’re not ready for Season 3 ,” Manganiello also teased elements of his real life throne room set that fans will get to see in the new season. But he’s only just one of the faces to keep an eye out for in the new episodes.

What’s New for Netflix’s One Piece Season 3

Joe Manganiello will be getting a much more expansive role in One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta when it comes to Netflix next year, and the same will be the case for other new additions seen in the second season like Mikaela Hoover as Tony Tony Chopper, Charithra Chandran as Princess Vivi, Sendhil Ramamurthy as Nefartari Cobra, and Lera Abova as Nico Robin. But there will be a ton of new faces that fans will get to meet as Alabasta offers a wide cast of characters as war breaks out over the entire region.

New additions to the cast for One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta include Xolo Maridueña as Ace , Cole Escola as Bon Clay, Awdo Awdo as Mr. 1, Daisy Head as Miss Doublefinger, Emilio Sakraya as Koza, Omid Abtahi as Toto, Jamie Ward as Pell, and Nabeel Khan as Chaka. More characters and cast members are likely going to be revealed as we get closer to the new season’s launch, but what are you hoping to see from Crocodile in Netflix’s One Piece? Let us know all of your thoughts in the comments!

title: Live-Action 5 Centimeters Per Second Film Opens in Indian Theaters on October 30
content:
The film opened in Japan in October 2025, and ranked at #2 in its opening weekend. The film sold 278,000 tickets and earned 420 million yen (about US$2.78 million) in its first three days.

SixTONES member Hokuto Matsumura ( Suzume 's Sōta Munakata) stars in the live-action film.

Spoon produced the film, and TOHO distributed. Yoshiyuki Okuyama directed, and Ayako Suzuki wrote the script. Ayatake Ezaki composed the music. Kenshi Yonezu performs the theme song "1991."

GKIDS released the film in North America and describes the film:

After transferring to the same elementary school, Takaki and Akari became best friends. However, their lives change when both their families are forced to relocate. After a year of separation, Takaki is about to reunite with Akari. As he sits on the train from Tokyo, memories of the past rush through Takaki's head, his meeting time with Akari drawing ever closer. Takaki and Akari begin to wonder if they will ever be able to see each other again, and share their secret feelings. Join Takaki on a journey into three interconnected tales of love and lost innocence that span the minutes and months of their lives.

The 5 Centimeters per Second anime opened in Japan in 2007.

Shinkai directed, wrote, and storyboarded the anime film, and was also the sound director, producer, and art director. Tenmon composed the music.

title: Anime Times Streams Nia Liston: The Merciless Maiden Anime in India
content:
Anime Times began streaming the television anime of Umikaze Minamino 's Nia Liston: The Merciless Maiden ( Kyōran Reijō Nia Liston: Byōjaku Reijō ni Tenseishita Kami-goroshi no Bujin no Kareinaru Musō Roku ) light novel series on Amazon Prime Video in India on Thursday.

The anime premiered on October 6 on Tokyo MX at 9:25 p.m. JST, then on the BS NTV , and MBS channels, and will run for two consecutive cours (quarters of a year). The anime streams in Japan on ABEMA , d Anime Store , and U-NEXT after its broadcast.

J-Novel Club releases the novels digitally and describes the story:

A great hero lies undefeated on her deathbed, regretting that she never found a foe who could take her down. She never intended to meet her fate anywhere other than on the battlefield, and her peaceful demise has her wishing desperately that things could have been different...But when she suddenly comes to in the body of the young, frail Nia Liston, she's got an all-new fight ahead of her. Nia is a sickly child, meaning she has a long way to go before she's in fighting form. Now that she's been given a second shot at life, however, she's determined to get what she wants. She's going to live—and die—for battle this time! Make way for the Merciless Maiden!

Motoki Nakanishi ( Love Is Indivisible by Twins , Summoned to Another World for a Second Time ) is directing the anime at KONAMI animation with Haruta Segi as the assistant director. Gigaemon Ichikawa ( Himitsu no AiPri , PuniRunes three seasons) is in charge of series scripts, Yūki Itō ( Mob Psycho 100 II OAV key animator) and Kana Tosaoka ( Kantai Collection -KanColle- film in-between animator) are designing the characters. Naoki Endō ( Love Live! Nijigasaki High School Idol Club , Nijiyon Animation ) is composing the music, and Hiromi Kikuta ( Aikatsu! , Blue Period , Haikyu!! ) is directing the sound.

VTuber Tsunomaki Watame performs the opening theme song "Respawn!!." Magic Vision Girls Party (Magic Vision Hirome-Tai) — the musical unit formed by the characters Nia Liston (voiced by Honoka Inoue ), Hildetora Altoir (voiced by Rina Honnizumi ), and Reliared Silver (voiced by Rina Hidaka ) — is performing the ending theme "Tokimeki Un ・Deux ・Trois♪" (Heart Fluttering 1, 2, 3♪).

Minamino launched the story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in 2019, and ended its run there in 2021. Hobby Japan started publishing the novels with illustration by Jishaku in September 2022. Katana Canata started drawing the novels' illustration from its third volume in 2023. (The anime credits both illustrators for the original character designs.) Hobby Japan published the 12th volume on October 1.

Kabuto Kodai launched the novels' manga adaptation on Square Enix 's Manga UP! service in 2022. Square Enix published the manga's first compiled book volume in May 2023, and published the ninth volume on October 7. Square Enix 's Manga UP! Global service publishes the manga in English.

title: Dandadan Studio’s Ghost in the Shell Reboot Confirmed to Continue With Sequel
content:
The new Ghost in the Shell reboot anime series from the s ame studio behind hits like DAN DA DAN has announced it’s now working on a new anime project for the franchise. Out of all the science fiction anime franchises out there, Masamune Shirow’s Ghost in the Shell is likely one of the most famous. Not only has it been adapted into ten different kind of anime projects at this point, but it’s also hit the big screen with notorious movie projects and more. Its reboot has been a hit outside of all of that, however.

Seemingly making up for the fact that the franchise has been on a downturn with its latest few anime efforts, The Ghost in the Shell made its debut earlier this Summer as one of the more well received reboot efforts of the franchise from longtime fans. That’s why it’s even better news to find out that Science SARU is now working on another new anime project for the Ghost in the Shell franchise. Check out the announcement poster for it below.

New The Ghost in the Shell Anime in Development From Science SARU

Bandai Namco Filmworks has officially announced that a new anime project for The Ghost in the Shell is now in the works, but has yet to confirm many details about what shape the new project will take. It will once again feature animation produced by Science SARU, but further production staff has yet to be announced. It’s not clear whether this project will be a new TV anime series, feature film, or even a potential OVA project, nor has it been revealed to be a sequel to the TV anime reboot that wrapped up its run earlier this Summer .

Either way, this is a great move for The Ghost in the Shell franchise. There have been so many different takes on it over the years that there also has been no unifying vision for these adaptations as a result. This new reboot has been a success with fans ever since it kicked off its run earlier this Summer , so any potential to continue that with new stories adding onto the foundation already set could be a great move forward. Especially considering it had Shirow’s seal of approval from the jump too.

What to Know for The Ghost in the Shell Reboot

If you missed out on The Ghost in the Shell’ s return to screens earlier this year for its new reboot, you can now find the entire debut season streaming exclusively with Prime Video. Directed by Moko-chan (their directorial debut) for Science SARU, the reboot series was a special collaboration between Bandai Namco Filmworks, Kodansha and Production I.G. Toh Enjoe handlded the scripts for the series, Shuhei Handa provided the character designs and served as chief animation director, and Ryo Konishi and Yuki Kanesaka composed the music.

There are potential routes the franchise can take if it decides to continue the reboot with a direct sequel story, but also other routes to take with something original next instead. What are you hoping to see from the Ghost in the Shell anime franchise next? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: 2025’s Darkest Anime Returns With New Movie This Fall – Watch the Trailer
content:
One of the darkest anime of the last year is coming back with a new feature film release later this Fall, and a new trailer is showing more of it off before it hits theaters across Japan. Crunchyroll has been home to some truly dark anime releases that have caught fans off guard in a few ways, and there’s probably no better example of this than with the anime adaptation for Taizan 5’s Takopi’s Original Sin . Now it’s coming back to break hearts all over again, but just on the big screen this time.

Takopi’s Original Sin The Movie: Thank You, See You Tomorrow is a new compilation film that repackages the six episode miniseries into a new feature film package with new materials teased for the upgrade. This new version of the anime is gearing up for its debut across theaters in Japan later this Fall, and a new trailer is helping to show off the best look at the anime yet. You can check it out along with a new poster you can find below.

Takopi’s Original Sin Movie Reveals New Trailer Ahead of Japan Launch

Takopi’s Original Sin The Movie: Thank You, See You Tomorrow is currently scheduled to hit theaters in Japan on November 27th , but no potential international release plans have been announced as of this time. The new film version features a returning staff from the TV anime series with Shinya Iino directing and handling the scripts for ENISHIYA, and Keita Nagahara providing the character designs. The main voice cast for the anime include Kurumi Mamiya as Takopi, Reina Ueda as Shizuka Kuze, Konomi Kohara as Marina, and Anna Nagase as Azuma.

Takopi’s Original Sin The Movie: Thank You, See You Tomorrow is a new compilation film retooling the events of the six episode miniseries adapting Taizan 5’s original manga. This new film is teased to be the most complete version of the story with new footage exclusive to the film version , and a new theme song for the overall package titled “Love You” as performed by Tele. But as for what new footage might be included in the experience, it’s still being kept a mystery as of this time.

What Is Takopi’s Original Sin & Why Is It So Dark?

Takopi’s Original Sin made its debut last Summer with a much different kind of anime experience than fans had ever expected when it was first made available for streaming with Crunchyroll . Not only did it have a much shorter run of episodes overall than every other anime seen last year, but its content was some of the darkest seen that year too. Dealing with some very real topics like child abuse, neglect, murder, suicide and more, it was all the more heartbreaking due to the very young characters at the center of these developments.

Takopi’s Original Sin might not have had as explosive of an anime debut as some of the other new anime releases fans had seen last year , but it had made a strong impact thanks to the number of intense sequences and moments throughout its run. It was one surprise after another, and this film version is likely going to take it all to the next level. Would you want to see the new Takopi’s Original Sin movie? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

Takopi’s Original Sin might not have had as explosive of an anime debut as some of the other new anime releases fans had seen last year , but it had made a strong impact thanks to the number of intense sequences and moments throughout its run.
